objective.text: Distinguish ShouldBroadcastNow from a queued ShouldBroadcast event.

difficulty.rationale: Predict the broadcast execution boundary under the two interfaces.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

assumptions: The normal queue is asynchronous; the broadcaster is configured and succeeds. No worker runs during the two dispatch calls.

stem: One event implements ShouldBroadcast and another implements ShouldBroadcastNow. What distinguishes their broadcast work when dispatched?

options.text: Both broadcast synchronously because events are never queued.
options.rationale: The normal ShouldBroadcast path uses a queued broadcast job.
options.misconception: The normal ShouldBroadcast path uses a queued broadcast job.

options.text: The first queues broadcast work; the second broadcasts synchronously.
options.rationale: ShouldBroadcastNow selects the immediate broadcast dispatch path instead of the normal queue.

options.text: The first broadcasts synchronously and the second waits for the next scheduler tick.
options.rationale: This reverses the first behavior and invents a scheduling requirement for the second.
options.misconception: This reverses the first behavior and invents a scheduling requirement for the second.

options.text: Both wait for a worker; Now only assigns higher queue priority.
options.rationale: Now changes the dispatch mode, not merely priority within an asynchronous queue.
options.misconception: Now changes the dispatch mode, not merely priority within an asynchronous queue.
